title: Mao's China

cards.h: The man who unified China, then lost track of how many he lost
cards.b:
On 1 October 1949, standing on Tiananmen, Mao Zedong announced the People's Republic of China. 'China has stood up,' he said, according to the common account.

He would rule for 27 years. The results were mixed and often terrible.
The Communists won the civil war against the Nationalists (Kuomintang), who fled to Taiwan. Land reform took land from landlords, and many were killed. China fought the US in Korea.

In 1958 Mao tried to leap into industry with village steel furnaces and giant communes. Bad planning, false harvest reports and forced grain collection caused a famine. Estimates of deaths run from about 15 to 45 million, commonly about 30 million. The exact number is debated.

Mao stepped back, but kept power.

In 1966 Mao urged young Red Guards to attack 'bourgeois' elements. Teachers, officials and intellectuals were beaten and humiliated. Schools closed. The Little Red Book of his quotes was waved by millions.

The army had to restore order, and the chaos ended with Mao's death on 9 September 1976.

Deng Xiaoping took over and launched reform and opening in 1978. The Communist Party itself, in 1981, judged Mao as 70 percent right and 30 percent wrong, though that figure is a Party formula. Mao's portrait still hangs on Tiananmen.

Supporters credit Mao with ending foreign domination, raising literacy and life expectancy. Critics (such as Frank Dikötter) stress the famine and terror. Both can be true. Estimates of famine deaths vary with the method.

A myth check: the 'Four Pests' campaign, including killing sparrows, did upset the ecosystem and probably worsened crop losses, but it was not the main cause of famine.

Five things to remember

  1. The PRC was founded on 1 October 1949.
  2. The Great Leap Forward (1958-62) caused famine.
  3. The Cultural Revolution lasted 1966-76.
  4. Deng began reform in 1978.
  5. The 1962 war shaped India-China ties.

Think about it

  • Can a leader's aims justify huge costs?
  • How did the 1962 war change India?
